english.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for an intentionally false statement.
This is the all-purpose colloquial noun for a falsehood or made-up claim.
Use this as the everyday all-purpose noun for an invented falsehood, especially one told to deceive.
Use this for a made-up or deliberately untrue account, rather than for the literary genre.
Pick 大話 when “nonsense” means a lie or a deliberately untrue statement.
Use 大話 when the “story” is a lie or made-up claim rather than a narrative.
Use this when the tale is specifically a lie or false account.

examples.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 gong2 daai6 waa6 laa3

examples.english: Your claim that you went there is a fabrication.
examples.traditional: 你話自己去過嗰度，根本係大話嚟㗎。
examples.jyutping: nei5 waa6 zi6 gei2 heoi3 gwo3 go2 dou6 gan1 bun2 hai6 daai6 waa6 lai4 gaa3

examples.english: They told a whole load of fabulation to cover up being late.
examples.traditional: 佢為咗掩飾遲到，講咗一大輪大話。

examples.english: I don't believe a word of the fiction you just made up.
examples.traditional: 你啱啱講嗰啲大話，我一句都唔信。
